prompt.brief: Design model serving infrastructure that exposes multiple ML frameworks through REST/gRPC, autoscaling GPU and CPU replicas, traffic splitting for canaries, and fast rollback based on health and quality signals.
successSignals: Make a signed deployment manifest authoritative for model digest, runtime, resource profile, routes, and rollout policy.
Use weighted, sticky, or request-segmented traffic splitting with warmup, shadowing, and automatic rollback gates.
Bound batching, queueing, feature lookups, and GPU memory; expose model and replica health separately from business quality.
Explain multi-framework adapters, autoscaling, cold starts, overload, privacy, canary bias, and failure recovery.

functional: Register model deployments, provision replicas, serve REST/gRPC predictions, split traffic, and promote or roll back versions.
Support batching, streaming responses, autoscaling, explainability, request limits, model-specific preprocessing, and health checks.
Expose latency, errors, queue time, throughput, resource use, canary quality, drift, and rollout decision history.
nonFunctional: Target p99 inference latency below 100 ms for warm replicas and keep canary overhead within the request budget.
Serve 100K requests per second across model versions with isolated queues and resource pools.
Make deployment, route changes, prediction logging, and rollback idempotent; never split traffic to an unready model.
Route to the last healthy version or return a bounded overload response when a pool or feature dependency fails.
scaleAssumptions: Operate 1,000 endpoints, 10,000 replicas, and 100K requests per second across CPU and GPU model pools.
Partition routing and telemetry by endpoint, model version, tenant, and region; isolate hot endpoints.
Retain signed deployment manifests, sampled predictions, rollout decisions, and health history while bounding logs.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Model serving infrastructure commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Model serving infrastructure writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Model serving infrastructure version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Model serving infrastructure by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Model serving infrastructure work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Model serving infrastructure projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Model serving infrastructure projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Model serving infrastructure records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Model serving infrastructure latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
